macro_markets.query: What are the most important macroeconomic and stock market news and developments from the past 24 hours? Include major index movements, Fed/central bank news, and significant company earnings or announcements.

items.title: Wall Street rallies as AI optimism returns and Treasury yields ease
items.summary: U.S. stocks surged Monday, with the S&P 500 and Nasdaq posting sharp gains as investors rotated back into AI-heavy names such as AMD. Lower Treasury yields and falling crude prices also helped sentiment, while the Nasdaq hit a record high in some reports.

items.title: Bank of Canada warns new U.S. tariffs could hurt growth
items.summary: Bank of Canada Governor Tiff Macklem said new U.S. tariffs could cut Canada’s fourth-quarter growth to below 1%, citing uncertainty around investment and hiring. The warning underscores rising trade-policy risks for the Canadian economy.

items.title: Fed official says fighting inflation may require economic pain
items.summary: A top Federal Reserve official said the central bank may need to accept higher unemployment to fully bring down stubborn inflation. The remarks reinforced expectations that policy may stay restrictive or tighten further.

items.title: China keeps benchmark lending rates unchanged for 16th straight month
items.summary: The People’s Bank of China left its one-year and five-year loan prime rates unchanged, signaling caution despite ongoing economic support needs. Chinese equities rose modestly after the decision, helped by AI-related demand and optimism around U.S.-China engagement.

items.title: U.S. futures rise as oil drops and rate expectations shift
items.summary: U.S. stock futures moved higher Monday as oil prices fell and Treasury yields slipped below the closely watched 5% level. Markets continued to price in a meaningful chance of another Fed rate hike next month, while China also held rates steady.

items.title: Dow, S&P 500 and Nasdaq all close higher on AI-led buying
items.summary: The Dow rose 0.71%, the S&P 500 gained 1.49%, and the Nasdaq jumped 2.26% in Monday trading, with AI stocks driving much of the advance. Falling oil prices and lower Treasury yields were key macro supports for the rally.

items.title: Oil prices extend slide on hopes for Middle East progress
items.summary: Crude fell sharply, with WTI dipping below $94 in some reports as traders reacted to signs of possible progress in Middle East negotiations and higher Saudi supply. The decline in oil helped ease pressure on inflation and bond yields.

items.title: China-U.S. talks and summit hopes support risk appetite
items.summary: Markets were lifted by optimism around high-level U.S.-China engagement ahead of a closely watched Trump-Xi summit. The improving diplomatic tone helped Chinese equities and U.S. futures, especially technology shares tied to AI demand.

items.title: Gold slips as rate-hike odds and stronger dollar weigh
items.summary: Gold edged lower as traders priced in a higher chance of further Fed tightening and the dollar strengthened. The move reflected a broader market shift toward tighter financial conditions and away from safe-haven demand.

crypto_news.query: What are the most significant cryptocurrency and blockchain news from the past 24 hours? Include major price movements, regulatory news, and notable project developments.

items.title: Bitcoin jumps above $85,000 as short liquidations fuel a broad crypto rebound
items.summary: Bitcoin climbed above $85,000 in a sharp 24-hour rally, with several reports attributing the move to a short squeeze and strong market-wide liquidations. Ethereum, XRP, Solana, and Dogecoin also posted solid gains as the broader crypto market rose toward $3 trillion in value.

items.title: SEC tokenized-stocks move boosts risk appetite across crypto markets
items.summary: Cryptocurrencies rallied after the SEC introduced a regulatory pathway allowing certain tokenized U.S. stocks to trade on blockchain platforms. Market commentary linked the policy shift to gains in Bitcoin, Ethereum, XRP, Dogecoin, and altcoins such as NEAR and Avalanche.

items.title: Bitcoin approaches $84,000 as oil weakness lifts risk assets
items.summary: Bitcoin traded just under $84,000 and remained up nearly 2% over 24 hours, extending a recent climb. Ethereum, Solana, XRP, and Dogecoin also advanced, while Monero briefly outperformed large-cap tokens with a double-digit move.

items.title: Altcoins lead the rally as NEAR, Avalanche, and The Graph outpace Bitcoin
items.summary: Altcoins were the main drivers of the latest crypto rally, with NEAR Protocol, Avalanche, and The Graph among the strongest performers over 24 hours. The report also noted fresh momentum from SEC and CFTC regulatory developments and renewed interest in Ethereum infrastructure proposals.

items.title: Ethereum rises after Bitcoin-led short squeeze wipes out more than $700 million
items.summary: Ethereum gained roughly 6% as a Bitcoin-led short squeeze triggered more than $700 million in crypto liquidations over 24 hours. The move was part of a broader rebound that lifted major tokens and intensified volatility across the market.

items.title: SEC and CFTC regulatory actions drive tokenization and market-structure optimism
items.summary: Reports say the SEC approved a temporary five-year exemption for tokenized-stock trading on selected blockchain platforms, while the CFTC sent draft crypto-market rules to the White House. Traders and analysts said the combination of measures helped support the latest altcoin rotation and broad market gains.

items.title: NEAR jumps on swap traffic as altcoin rotation intensifies
items.summary: NEAR emerged as one of the standout winners, rising about 23% as swap activity increased. The report also highlighted gains in ZEC, BNB, ETH, HYPE, XRP, DOGE, SOL, and TRX as Bitcoin held above $81,000.

items.title: RENDER surges 16% as traders rotate into altcoins
items.summary: Render posted a strong 24-hour gain and saw trading volume more than triple, making it one of the most notable project-level movers in the latest session. The move was described as part of a broader rotation into altcoins.

ai_news.query: What are the most important artificial intelligence and machine learning news and developments from the past 24 hours? Include new model releases, company announcements, research breakthroughs, and industry trends.

items.title: U.S. proposes AI incident alert system with China
items.summary: Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent said the U.S. is proposing a notification mechanism for AI incidents with China, aimed at reducing national-security risks from advanced AI systems. The proposal adds a diplomacy-and-safety dimension to the U.S.-China AI competition.

items.title: OpenAI discloses new framework for tracking concerning model behavior
items.summary: OpenAI said it has disclosed six reports of unexpected or concerning model behavior and is introducing a framework to document and monitor what it calls misalignment. The disclosure underscores growing industry focus on safety, oversight, and model behavior in deployed systems.

items.title: Anthropic says Claude is helping build the next version of itself
items.summary: Anthropic said its model Claude is being used to help develop the next iteration of the model, highlighting a growing trend toward AI-assisted AI research and engineering. The development reflects how leading labs are increasingly using models in their own development pipelines.

items.title: Lawsuit accuses Anthropic, OpenAI, SpaceXAI, and Google of coordinating an AI slowdown
items.summary: A newly filed antitrust complaint alleges that major AI companies illegally agreed to slow AI development, reducing consumer value for paid subscriptions. The case adds to mounting legal and regulatory pressure around competition in the AI sector.

items.title: Trump announces an 'AI Force' and a new AI czar search
items.summary: Donald Trump said the U.S. would create an 'AI Force' and appoint a new AI czar, signaling a pro-growth policy posture rather than a slowdown. The announcement comes amid broader political debate over AI safety, regulation, and national competitiveness.

items.title: AI safety debate intensifies as major tech leaders split over development pace
items.summary: Reuters reported that AI leaders remain divided, with some calling for a coordinated slowdown while others favor market-led safeguards. The split shows that safety concerns, governance, and competitive pressure are now central industry issues.

items.title: Linear says AI coding agents forced major CI infrastructure changes
items.summary: Linear published engineering details showing that AI-generated code increased CI bottlenecks, prompting tooling and runner changes that cut runner time and improved job performance. The report illustrates how AI adoption is already reshaping software development workflows.

items.title: New compact text-to-image model released after very short H100 training run
items.summary: SupraLabs open-released Supra2-IMG, a 100M-parameter text-to-image model that the team says was trained from scratch in under 10 hours on a single H100 GPU. If validated, the release points to continued efficiency gains in small-model image generation.

gaming.query: What are the most notable video game and gaming industry news from the past 24 hours? Include game releases, announcements, esports, and industry developments.

items.title: Xbox showcases 17 games at Tokyo Game Show, including major reveals and Game Pass additions
items.summary: Microsoft’s Tokyo Game Show presentation featured 17 games, with notable updates on Call of Duty: Modern Warfare 4, Fallout 76’s The Slasher update, Bloodstained: The Scarlet Engagement, and multiple Xbox Game Pass announcements. The event also highlighted new footage for several Japanese and indie projects.

items.title: Bungie says it will restore vaulted Destiny 2 content and rework Marathon
items.summary: Game Informer reports that Bungie is planning to bring back vaulted Destiny 2 content while also making substantial changes to Marathon. The move appears aimed at rebuilding player trust after recent backlash.

items.title: Hideo Kojima details the scramble that led Physint to Xbox backing
items.summary: Game Developer reports that Kojima Productions had to urgently find a new publisher after Sony ended funding support for Physint. The project ultimately landed with Microsoft-owned Xbox.

items.title: Xbox highlights nearly 40 games arriving this week in Microsoft Store
items.summary: A roundup from iXBT Games says Microsoft Store is set to receive almost 40 releases this week, including Dune: Awakening, Graveyard Keeper 2, CONTROL Resonant, and EA SPORTS FC 27. This points to a busy release slate across multiple genres.

items.title: We Were Here Tomorrow gets October release date with cross-platform support
items.summary: Báhamut GNN reports that We Were Here Tomorrow will launch on October 20 for Steam, PlayStation 5, and Xbox Series X|S. The co-op puzzle adventure will support cross-platform play at launch.
